div.head: Ps Cn for 11
div.ab: Habeantque hii quatuor unam regalem potestatem, salua nobis nostra presentia; quaterque in anno generales foreste demonstrationes et uiridis et ueneris forisfactiones, quas muchimut dicunt, teneant, ubi omnes calumnia[ti] de materia aliqua tangente forestam eant ad triplex iudicium, quod Angli ofgan ꝥ ordel dicunt.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 622 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: And let these four have a royal power, saving to us our presence; and four times a year let them hold general views of the forest and [pleas of] offences of both vert and venison, which they call muchimut (great moot), where all who are accus[ed] in any matter touching the forest shall go to the threefold ordeal, which the English call ofgan ꝥ ordel (to obtain the ordeal).

note.seg: Königlich heisst im 12. Jh. das staatliche Gericht (s. d. Gl 10) auch in der Provinz, vor öffentlichen Lokalbeamten oder reisenden Königsrichtern; s. d. Gl 3a
In the 12th century the public court is called royal (see that word in Gl 10) in the provinces too, before public local officials or itinerant royal justices; see that word in Gl 3a
Die vier Gerichtszeiten entnahm Verf. vielleicht denen des Reichsgerichts, die vór 1194 nachweisbar sind; Maitland Three rolls of the King’s court p. xiv
The author perhaps took the four court sessions from those of the king’s central court, which are attested before 1194; Maitland Three rolls of the King’s court p. xiv
Swanimot kommt vor für höhere Forstenquête im 13. Jh.
Swanimot occurs for a higher forest inquest in the 13th century
